324	## JSON Structure
325	
326	The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
327	
328	```json
329	{
330	  "id": "autonomousAgent1",
331	  "type": "uipath.agent.autonomous",
332	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
333	  "display": { "label": "Autonomous Agent" },
334	  "inputs": {
335	    "systemPrompt": "You are an agentic assistant.",
336	    "userPrompt": "What is the current date?",
337	    "source": "<projectId-uuid>",
338	    "agentInputVariables": [],
339	    "agentOutputVariables": [
340	      { "id": "content", "type": "string" }
341	    ]
342	  },
343	  "outputs": {
344	    "error": {
345	      "type": "object",
346	      "description": "Error information if the node fails",
347	      "source": "=Error",
348	      "var": "error"
349	    }
350	  }
351	}
352	```
353	
354	Notes:
355	
356	- `inputs.source` — the inline agent's `projectId`; must match the subdirectory name and `agent.json.projectId`. The definition still declares `model.source: true`, but flow-core hoists that identity field onto `inputs.source` for the node instance.
357	- `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` must be non-empty for current `flow validate`. Treat them as validator placeholders; the canonical inline-agent prompts live in `agent.json`.
358	- `inputs.agentInputVariables` carries one entry per flow input the agent reads — `{ id: "<trigger>__output__<var>", binding: "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. This is the only thing the converter turns into the runtime `JobArguments`; prompts then reference each input as `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` (see § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts above). Leave it `[]` only when the agent reads no flow data.
359	- **No `model` block on the inline-agent node instance.** The node inherits serviceType/version/context from `definitions[]`; `source` lives at `inputs.source`. Stale instance fields such as `model.serviceType`, `model.version`, or `model.context` override the inherited definition and can cause runtime mismatch.
360	
361	## Accessing Output
362	
363	How agent output surfaces depends on `agent.json` `outputSchema`:
364	
365	- **Typed `outputSchema`** (the required form — step 5) — each property surfaces **flat** at `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>`. For `outputSchema.properties` `{ subject, body }`: read `$vars.<nodeId>.output.subject` and `$vars.<nodeId>.output.body`. **There is no `.content.` wrapper** — `$vars.<nodeId>.output.content.subject` resolves to undefined and silently yields a null flow output.
366	- **Untyped (single string)** — only when no typed schema is declared: `$vars.<nodeId>.output.content` holds the agent's text response.
367	- `$vars.<nodeId>.error` — error details if the agent fails.
368	
369	To expose a typed field as a flow output, see § Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs below.
370	
371	## Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs
372	
373	Symmetric to input wiring — **three aligned pieces**, none CLI-derived:
374	
375	| Where | What | Example |
376	| --- | --- | --- |
377	| `agent.json` `outputSchema.properties` | One typed key per field the agent returns. | `"subject": { "type": "string" }`, `"body": { "type": "string" }` |
378	| Flow node `inputs.agentOutputVariables[]` | **One entry per field** — NOT a single `content` object. | `[{ "id": "subject", "type": "string" }, { "id": "body", "type": "string" }]` |
379	| End node `outputs.<global>` | Maps each `out` global to the flat field path. | `"emailBody": { "source": "=js:$vars.<agentNodeId>.output.body" }` |
380	
381	Plus: declare each flow output as a `direction: "out"` global in `variables.globals[]`, and map it on **every reachable End node**.
382	
383	**Anti-pattern:** `agentOutputVariables: [{ "id": "content", "type": "object" }]` paired with End `=js:$vars.<node>.output.content.<field>`. The typed agent delivers fields flat at `output.<field>`; the `.content.` path resolves to undefined → `flow validate` passes, debug Completes, but the flow output is **null**.
384	
385	## Refresh and Validate
386	
387	Refresh the inline agent (writes `entry-points.json` and `bindings_v2.json`, and for tool-bearing agents, propagates bindings into the flow project's `bindings_v2.json`), then validate (read-only check), then validate the flow:
388	
389	```bash
390	# 1. Refresh the inline agent (writes entry-points.json and bindings_v2.json)
391	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
392	
393	# 1b. For tool-bearing inline agents, refresh with --bindings-target to propagate tool bindings:
394	uip agent refresh "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow \
395	  --bindings-target "<FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json" --output json
396	
397	# 2. Validate the inline agent (read-only schema check)
398	uip agent validate "<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>" --inline-in-flow --output json
399	
400	# 3. Validate the flow
401	uip maestro flow validate <FlowName>.flow --output json
402	```
403	
404	> Current validator requirement: `uip maestro flow validate` rejects flows whose `uipath.agent.autonomous` node lacks non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt`. Include placeholder values on the flow node, but keep the canonical prompts in the inline agent's `agent.json`.
405	
406	> **Refresh also shell-ifies the parent `.flow` (self-contained flows).** When a flow was authored self-contained in Studio Web, its `.flow` embeds the inline agent's prompts/model/guardrails and each resource node's config **inline** (not just in the `<projectId>/` sidecar). Since you edit the **sidecar**, that stale embed would shadow your edits when the flow is re-opened in Studio Web (the embed wins over the sidecar on load). So `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` strips this agent's embedded config back out of the parent `.flow` — leaving only structural inputs (`source`, `agentInputVariables`, etc.) on the agent node and `{source, detail, itemsDescription}` on its resource nodes — so Studio Web re-hydrates the cluster from your freshly-written sidecar on import. It is **scoped to the agent being refreshed** (siblings untouched), a **no-op** for flows authored from scratch via the CLI (already shells), and **best-effort** (a failure never fails refresh). When it acts, the JSON output carries `FlowShellified: true` and `FlowResourceNodesStripped: <n>`. You author the sidecar (`agent.json` + `resources/`); refresh keeps the `.flow` a shell — do not hand-embed prompts/config back into the flow node.
407	
408	## Debug
409	
410	| Error | Cause | Fix |
411	| --- | --- | --- |
412	| `flow validate` reports `systemPrompt` / `userPrompt` required | The flow node lacks non-empty validator placeholders, the `inputs.source` UUID is missing, or the inline agent subdirectory cannot be found | Add non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` placeholders, set `inputs.source` to the inline agent UUID, and verify `<FlowDir>/<projectId>/agent.json` exists |
413	| `inputs.source` UUID does not match any subdirectory | Wrong source value, or folder renamed | Set `inputs.source` to the exact UUID of the inline agent directory |
414	| Flow runs a different agent than expected | `inputs.source` points to a stale/leftover inline agent dir | Check subdirectory names — only one inline agent dir should correspond to each agent node |
415	| `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob` error at runtime | Stale instance `model` fields override the inherited inline-agent definition | Remove the inline-agent node's instance `model` block and keep the registry definition's `model.serviceType: "Orchestrator.StartInlineAgentJob"` in `definitions[]` |
416	| Studio Web reports "System prompt is required" | Inline agent's `agent.json.messages[]` has empty `content`, OR derived files (`entry-points.json`, `bindings_v2.json`) are stale | Set prompts in `agent.json`, re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` to regenerate derived files, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check — see `uipath-agents` skill |
417	| Studio Web debug: "Could not find process for tool" | Flow project's `bindings_v2.json` is missing the tool's process binding, so `uip solution resources refresh` never created the solution-level resource | Re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` to propagate bindings, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check schema, then `uip solution resources refresh`, then re-upload |
418	| `bindings_v2.json` is empty or missing tool bindings | Tool bindings were not propagated to the flow project level, or a later tool overwrote the file | Re-run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` after all flow node and edge edits are complete. Refresh is the verb that writes the file — do not hand-edit it |
419	| Agent tool (process / agent / api / processOrchestration) cannot resolve at runtime | Missing top-level `bindings[]` entries, mismatched tool-node `inputs.source` / `resource.json` id, stale solution resources, or missing project-level `bindings_v2.json` | Add the resource bindings from the tool definition, keep the tool node's `inputs.source` equal to the resource UUID, run `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow --bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` to write bindings, then `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow` to check, then run `uip solution resources refresh` |
420	| `inputs.agentProjectId` unrecognized | Wrong field name | Use `inputs.source` — `agentProjectId` is not valid for inline agents |
421	| Inline agent rejected by `uip agent validate` | `entry-points.json` or `project.uiproj` present inside the inline agent dir | Delete those files — they belong only to standalone agent projects |
422	| Folder name is human-readable instead of UUID | Folder renamed after scaffolding | Rename to the original `projectId` UUID — the folder name must match `inputs.source` and the `projectId` field inside `agent.json` |
423	| Agent runs but returns empty `output.content` | Missing or malformed `contentTokens` in `agent.json` | Rebuild `messages[].contentTokens` using `{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "..." }` entries; see `uipath-agents` for detail |
424	| `flow validate` passes, debug Completes, but the `out` global (e.g. `emailBody`) is null | Typed agent output read with a `.content.` wrapper — `agentOutputVariables:[{content}]` + End `=js:$vars.<node>.output.content.<field>` — but typed fields surface flat at `output.<field>` | List each field in `agentOutputVariables[]` (`{id:"subject"},{id:"body"}`) and map End to `=js:$vars.<node>.output.<field>` (no `.content.`). See § Wiring Agent Output Into Flow Outputs. |
425	| `agent validate` flags `Expected type "simpleText" but got "text"` | Hand-edited `contentToken` written with `type: "text"` | Re-run `uip agent refresh` — it regenerates `contentTokens` from `content` (correct `simpleText`/`variable` types). Don't hand-edit the token. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
426	| `agent validate` flags `Expected "input.X" but got "{{input.X}}"` | Hand-edited `variable` token has the braces/extra spaces in its `rawString` | Re-run `uip agent refresh` to regenerate the tokens from `content` (brace-free `rawString`) — don't hand-fix it. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
427	| `agent validate` flags `contentTokens has N entries but content requires M. Rebuild contentTokens to match content.` | `content` and `contentTokens` drifted (e.g. tokens edited without `content`, or vice versa) | Re-run `uip agent refresh` to regenerate `contentTokens` from `content`. If the prompt itself is wrong, fix `content` first, then refresh. See § The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant. |
428	| Prompt shows literal `{{input.X}}` at runtime | `inputSchema.properties` missing the referenced key (`flow validate` flags this — run it) | Add the `<trigger>__output__<var>` key to `inputSchema`. |
429	| `flow validate` passes but debug faults `AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR` (literal `input.<key>`) | Node `agentInputVariables` uses `value:` instead of `binding:` (or is missing) → empty `JobArguments` | Set `binding:"=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>"` on the node entry; ensure the trigger global is declared (`direction:"in"`). |
430	| Debug faults `AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR` "Template placeholders detected instead of actual values" — and the node *does* have `agentInputVariables[]` | Entries use `value: "=js:$vars…"` (Studio Web's canvas form) instead of `binding`; the converter only reads `binding`, so `JobArguments` are empty | Rename `value` → `binding` on each entry and strip the `=js:` prefix: `{ "id": "<key>", "binding": "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. See § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts. |
431	
432	## Repair Recipes
433	
434	Use direct JSON edits for inline-agent graph repairs. The Flow CLI has no node-update command (see [editing-operations-cli.md § Operations Not Supported by CLI](../../editing-operations-cli.md#operations-not-supported-by-cli)), and the inline-agent graph is not a Flow CLI carve-out. If a bulk scripted rewrite is explicitly approved, use the `python3` heredoc pattern from [editing-operations-json.md — Edit Tooling](../../editing-operations-json.md#edit-tooling); otherwise apply the same transformations through `Edit` / `Write`.
435	
436	### Replace a definition entry
437	
438	Use when the `definitions[]` entry for a node type is wrong, stale, or hand-written. The fix is always: re-fetch from the registry, splice into `definitions[]` matching on `nodeType`, then keep the node instance minimal.
439	
440	```bash
441	uip maestro flow registry get uipath.agent.autonomous --output json > /tmp/registry_response.json
442	python3 - <<'PY'
443	import json
444	new_def = json.load(open("/tmp/registry_response.json"))["Data"]["Node"]
445	flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
446	for i, d in enumerate(flow["definitions"]):
447	    if d.get("nodeType") == "uipath.agent.autonomous":
448	        flow["definitions"][i] = new_def
449	        break
450	INLINE_TYPES = ("uipath.agent.autonomous", "uipath.agent.resource.")
451	for node in flow["nodes"]:
452	    t = node.get("type", "")
453	    if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
454	        model = node.pop("model", None) or {}
455	        if isinstance(model.get("source"), str):
456	            node.setdefault("inputs", {})["source"] = model["source"]
457	json.dump(flow, open("<FILE>.flow", "w"), indent=2)
458	PY
459	uip maestro flow validate <FILE>.flow --output json
460	```
461	
462	Same pattern works for any node type — substitute the `nodeType` string in both the `registry get` command and the loop guard. The `model.source` → `inputs.source` rewrite above is applied to both the inline agent node and every attached resource node (tool, escalation, context) — all of them carry source identity at `inputs.source` and never on an instance `model` block.
463	
464	### Resolve a `[REQUIRED_FIELD] systemPrompt is required` validator error
465	
466	Current flow validation requires non-empty placeholder prompts on the flow node and uses the inline agent directory referenced by `inputs.source`. Check in order:
467	
468	1. **UUID at `inputs.source`** — the `projectId` UUID must be set at `inputs.source`. Diagnose:
469	
470	    ```bash
471	    python3 - <<'PY'
472	    import json
473	    flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
474	    for node in flow["nodes"]:
475	        t = node.get("type", "")
476	        if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
477	            print(t, "inputs.source:", node.get("inputs", {}).get("source"))
478	            print(t, "model.source: ", node.get("model", {}).get("source"))
479	    PY
480	    ```
481	
482	    If a stale flow has the UUID at `model.source` on the inline agent node **or any attached resource node** (tool, escalation, context), move it to `inputs.source` and remove the instance `model` block:
483	
484	    ```bash
485	    python3 - <<'PY'
486	    import json
487	    flow = json.load(open("<FILE>.flow"))
488	    for node in flow["nodes"]:
489	        t = node.get("type", "")
490	        if t == "uipath.agent.autonomous" or t.startswith("uipath.agent.resource."):
491	            inputs = node.setdefault("inputs", {})
492	            model = node.pop("model", None) or {}
493	            uuid = model.get("source")
494	            if uuid:
495	                inputs["source"] = uuid
496	    json.dump(flow, open("<FILE>.flow", "w"), indent=2)
497	    PY
498	    ```
499	
500	2. **Subdirectory** — confirm `<FlowDir>/<projectId>/` exists and contains `agent.json`. If not, re-run `uip agent init "<FlowDir>" --inline-in-flow --output json` and bind the returned `ProjectId` through `inputs.source`.
501	
502	3. **Prompts in `agent.json`** — set `messages[0].content` (system) and `messages[1].content` (user) to real prompts before validate. Rebuild `messages[].contentTokens` to match — `[{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "<your prompt text>" }]` per message.
503	
504	4. **Validator placeholders on the flow node** — add non-empty `inputs.systemPrompt` and `inputs.userPrompt` placeholders if they are missing. These are for current `flow validate`; keep the canonical prompt text in `agent.json`.
505	
506	## What NOT to Do
507	
508	- **Do not use Flow CLI `node add`, `edge add`, or `variable` commands for inline-agent graph edits** — inline-agent node, edge, variable, layout, and tool-resource node changes are non-carve-out structural `.flow` mutations and must be authored directly with `Edit` / `Write`.
509	- **Do not treat `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` as canonical prompts** — current validation requires non-empty placeholders on the flow node, but prompts live in `agent.json`.
510	- **Do not put a `model` block on the inline-agent node instance** — the node inherits serviceType/version/context from `definitions[]`; the inline-agent source lives at `inputs.source`.
511	- **Do not use `model.agentProjectId`, `inputs.agentProjectId`, or `model.source` on any inline-agent-related node instance** — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached resource node (`uipath.agent.resource.tool.*`, `uipath.agent.resource.escalation`, `uipath.agent.resource.context.*`) carry source identity at `inputs.source` and have no instance `model` block.
512	- **Do not create `entry-points.json` or `project.uiproj` inside the inline agent directory** — those belong only to standalone agent projects.
513	- **Do not name the inline agent folder with a human-readable name** — the folder name must be the `projectId` UUID.
514	- **Do not use `uip agent tool add`** for inline-in-flow agents — hand-author the tool's `resource.json` instead.
515	- **Do not skip `uip agent refresh --inline-in-flow` followed by `uip agent validate --inline-in-flow`** after editing `agent.json` or any `resources/*/resource.json`; for tool-bearing inline agents, pass `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json` on the refresh call to propagate tool bindings.
516

1	# Agent Node — Planning
2	
3	Agent nodes invoke UiPath AI agents from within a flow. Published agents appear in the registry after `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`. **In-solution** (unpublished) agents in sibling projects are discovered via `--local` — no login or publish required. Both **coded** (Python) and **low-code** (agent.json) agents appear here once deployed — the flow treats them identically.
4	
5	> **Related plugin:** [inline-agent](../inline-agent/planning.md) covers low-code agents embedded as a UUID subdirectory **inside** the flow project (`uipath.agent.autonomous`). Coded agents always use this `agent` plugin, not `inline-agent`.
6	
7	> **Choosing between coded and low-code, or wiring them into a flow:** see the `uipath-agents` skill — [coded-vs-lowcode-guide.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded-vs-lowcode-guide.md) for the comparison, [coded/flow-integration.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/flow-integration.md) for coded-agent Flow patterns.
8	
9	> **If the user names an existing agent, it is a published agent — not inline.** When a prompt says "use the X agent" / "call the Y agent" / "invoke the Z coded agent" / "use the W low-code agent", the user is referring to an agent that already exists in the tenant (or in-solution). ALWAYS run `uip maestro flow registry search "<name>" --output json` BEFORE deciding to scaffold an inline agent. The words "coded" and "low-code" describe the *implementation style* of a published agent — they do NOT mean "inline". Inline (`uipath.agent.autonomous`) is only correct when the user explicitly asks to embed, inline, or create a new agent from scratch inside this flow.
10	
11	## Node Type Pattern
12	
13	`uipath.core.agent.{key}`
14	
15	The `{key}` is the agent's unique identifier (typically a GUID) from Orchestrator.
16	
17	## When to Use
18	
19	Use an Agent node when the flow needs to invoke a published AI agent for reasoning, judgment, or natural language processing.
20	
21	### Agent vs Script/Decision Decision Table
22	
23	| Use an Agent node when... | Use Script/Decision/Switch when... |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| Input is ambiguous or unstructured (free text, emails, support tickets) | Input is structured and well-defined (JSON, form data) |
26	| Task requires reasoning or judgment (triage, classification, summarization) | Task is deterministic (if X then Y, map/filter/transform) |
27	| Branching depends on context that can't be reduced to simple conditions | Branching conditions are explicit and enumerable |
28	| You need natural language generation (draft emails, summaries) | You need data transformation or computation |
29	
30	### Anti-Pattern
31	
32	Don't use an agent node for tasks that can be done with a Decision + Script. Agents are slower, more expensive (LLM tokens), and less predictable. Use them where their flexibility is actually needed.
33	
34	### Hybrid Pattern
35	
36	Use workflow nodes for the deterministic parts (fetch data, transform, route) and agent nodes for the ambiguous parts (classify intent, draft response, extract entities). The flow orchestrates; the agent reasons.
37	
38	### When NOT to Use
39	
40	- **Agent in the same solution but not yet published** — use `--local` discovery (see below)
41	- **Agent does not exist yet** — tell the user to create it in the same solution with `uipath-agents`, then use `--local` discovery
42	- **Task is deterministic** — use [Script](../script/planning.md) or [Decision](../decision/planning.md)
43	- **Need to call an external service API** — use [Connector](../connector/planning.md) or [HTTP](../http/planning.md)
44	- **Agent should be a tool for another agent** — don't use this node; instead add the agent as a tool resource (`uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent`) wired to a parent agent node. See the `uipath-agents` skill for the resource file format
45	
46	## Ports
47	
48	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
49	| --- | --- |
50	| `input` | `output`, `error` |
51	
52	The `error` port is the implicit error port shared with all action nodes — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
53	
54	## Output Variables
55	
56	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — the agent's response (contains `content` string)
57	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the agent fails (`code`, `message`, `detail`, `category`, `status`)
58

61	**Published (tenant registry):**
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
65	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent" --output json
66	```
67	
68	Requires `uip login`. Returns published tenant resources only — for in-solution sibling projects, use the `--local` discovery below.
69	
70	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
71	
72	```bash
73	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
74	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
75	```
76	
77	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling agent projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
78	
79	## Planning Annotation
80	
81	In the architectural plan:
82	- If the agent exists: note as `resource: <agent-name> (agent)`
83	- If it does not exist: note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` with skill `uipath-agents`

1	# Agent Node — Implementation
2	
3	Agent nodes invoke UiPath AI agents via node type `uipath.core.agent.{key}`. Coded (Python) agents always use this plugin; low-code (`agent.json`) agents use it only when they are a standalone project (in-solution sibling or published). Inline low-code agents (embedded as a UUID subdirectory inside the flow project) use `uipath.agent.autonomous` — see the [inline-agent plugin](../inline-agent/impl.md).
4	
5	The agent lives in one of two places:
6	
7	- **In this solution** — sibling project inside the current solution. `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution projects add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`). The runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API after `uip solution upload`. The manifest in `definitions[]` carries `model.section: "In this solution"`.
8	- **Published** — deployed to Orchestrator as a tenant resource. `{key}` is the Orchestrator-assigned resource key. Discoverable via `uip maestro flow registry search`. The manifest in `definitions[]` carries `model.section: "Published"`.
9	
10	The node-instance shape (in `nodes[]`) is identical across the two variants — only the manifest in `definitions[]` differs (`{key}` and `model.section`).
11	
12	## Discovery
13	
14	**Published (tenant registry):**
15	
16	```bash
17	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
18	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent" --output json
19	```
20	
21	Requires `uip login`. Only published agents from your tenant appear.
22	
23	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
24	
25	```bash
26	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
27	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
28	```
29	
30	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling agent projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
31	
32	## Registry Validation
33	
34	```bash
35	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.{key}" --output json
36	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.{key}" --local --output json
37	```
38	
39	Requires `uip login`. Only published agents from the tenant appear in the registry.
40	
41	Confirm from `registry get`:
42	
43	- Input port: `input`
44	- Output port: `output`
45	- `outputDefinition.output.schema` — contains `content` (string)
46	- `outputDefinition.error.schema` — contains `code`, `message`, `detail`, `category`, `status`
47	- `model.serviceType` — `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`
48	- `model.bindings.resourceSubType` — `Agent`
49	- `model.bindings.resourceKey` — the `<FolderPath>.<AgentName>` string used to scope binding resolution
50	- `inputDefinition` — typically empty (agents accept free-form input via the flow's wiring)
51	
52	## Adding / Editing
53	
54	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure below for the node-specific `inputs`.
55	
56	## JSON Structure
57	
58	### Node instance (inside `nodes[]`) — published variant
59	
60	The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and binding/context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "id": "classifyIntent",
65	  "type": "uipath.core.agent.ffa33d88-8a85-4570-933c-9a69aa2dfbb5",
66	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
67	  "display": { "label": "Classify Intent" },
68	  "inputs": {},
69	  "outputs": {
70	    "error": {
71	      "type": "object",
72	      "description": "Error information if the agent fails",
73	      "source": "=Error",
74	      "var": "error"
75	    }
76	  }
77	}
78	```
79	
80	The `model` block (BPMN type, `serviceType`, `bindings`, `context` template) lives on the manifest entry in `definitions[]`, not on the instance. The manifest is auto-populated by `uip maestro flow registry pull` — never hand-author it.
81	
82	Three values to discover — never invent:
83	- **`type` suffix** — Orchestrator-assigned UUID for this agent. Per-ring and per-agent — never copy across environments. Read from `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` / `registry get` as `nodeType`.
84	- **`typeVersion`** — the manifest's `version` field. Read from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json` (`.version`).
85	- **`resourceKey`** — composite `<FolderPath>.<AgentName>` (e.g. `Shared.Apple Genius Agent`). Appears on each top-level `bindings[]` entry tied to this agent. Read from `registry get` (`model.bindings.resourceKey` on the manifest).
86	
87	Confirm all three from `registry get` before wiring.
88	
89	### Node instance (inside `nodes[]`) — in-solution variant
90	
91	```json
92	{
93	  "id": "codedAgent",
94	  "type": "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>",
95	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
96	  "display": { "label": "<Label>", "icon": "<AGENT_ICON>" },
97	  "inputs": {},
98	  "outputs": {
99	    "error": { "type": "object", "description": "Error information if the agent fails", "source": "=Error", "var": "error" }
100	  }
101	}
102	```
103	
104	**Declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** Authoring it makes the converter copy your `source` verbatim; `"=result.response"` then resolves to null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. See [file-format.md § Node outputs](../../../../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
105	
106	`<AGENT_ICON>` depends on the agent's implementation type: `"coded-agent"` for Python-coded agents, `"autonomous-agent"` for low-code (`agent.json`) agents. Detect the type by inspecting the sibling agent project directory: if `agent.json` exists at its root, use `"autonomous-agent"`; otherwise use `"coded-agent"`. Do NOT copy `.display.icon` from `uip maestro flow registry get --local` — that manifest returns `"coded-agent"` for every in-solution agent regardless of implementation type, and the value must be corrected here.
107	
108	Same shape as the published variant — no `model` on the instance.
109	
110	**Never hand-author the `definitions[]` entry.** Run `uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json`, extract the `Data.Node` object, and paste it verbatim into `definitions[]`. Constructing it by hand risks missing required validator fields (`model.section`, `runtimeConstraints`, `supportsErrorHandling`, etc.).
111	
112	`<resourceKey>` is the local `resource.key` written by `uip solution projects add` to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json` — read it from that file or from `uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json`. Read `<DEFINITION_VERSION>` from `uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json` (`.version`).
113	
114	### Top-level `bindings[]` entries (sibling of `nodes`/`edges`/`definitions`)
115	
116	**Rule.** Exactly one entry per `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)` pair. Multiple node instances referencing the same agent MUST reuse the same `bindings[].id` — never duplicate the entry.
117	
118	**Validate.** After writing the flow, group `bindings[]` by `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)`. Each group must have length 1. If any group has length > 1, deduplicate before saving.
119	
120	```json
121	"bindings": [
122	  {
123	    "id": "bClassifyIntentName",
124	    "name": "name",
125	    "type": "string",
126	    "resource": "process",
127	    "resourceKey": "<resourceKey>",
128	    "default": "<agent-name>",
129	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
130	    "resourceSubType": "Agent"
131	  },
132	  {
133	    "id": "bClassifyIntentFolderPath",
134	    "name": "folderPath",
135	    "type": "string",
136	    "resource": "process",
137	    "resourceKey": "<resourceKey>",
138	    "default": "<folder-path-or-empty>",
139	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
140	    "resourceSubType": "Agent"
141	  }
142	]
143	```
144	
145	> For the resolution mechanics and why these entries are required, see [file-format.md — Bindings](../../../../shared/file-format.md#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings).
146	
147	## Accessing Output
148	
149	The agent's response is available downstream:
150	
151	```javascript
152	// In a Script node after the agent
153	const response = $vars.classifyIntent.output.content;
154	return { classification: response };
155	```
156	
157	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` — the agent's text response
158	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the agent fails
159	
160	## If the Agent Does Not Exist Yet
161	
162	Create the agent first, then wire it. Three paths:
163	
164	- **In-solution (sibling project, coded or low-code)** — scaffold via `uipath-agents`, register with `uip solution projects add` to mint the local `resource.key`, then discover via `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. For the coded pipeline, see [coded/embedding-in-flows.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/embedding-in-flows.md).
165	- **Published coded agent** — `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`.
166	- **Published low-code agent** — `uip solution deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`.
167	
168	## Using an Agent as a Tool Resource
169	
170	To use a published agent (coded or low-code) as a **tool for another agent** rather than a standalone flow node, add it as a `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` resource node wired to the parent agent's `tool` handle. This lives within the agent's canvas, not at the top level of the flow.
171	
172	For the resource file format and wiring details, see the `uipath-agents` skill:
173	- Coded agents: [coded/flow-integration.md § Pattern 3](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/flow-integration.md#pattern-3-tool-resource-for-another-agent)
174	- Low-code agents: see the `uipath-agents` skill's low-code references.
175	
176	## Debug
177	
178	| Error | Cause | Fix |
179	| --- | --- | --- |
180	| Node type not found in registry | Agent not published, or registry stale | If in same solution: run `registry list --local`. Otherwise: run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`. For coded agents, ensure `uip codedagent deploy` completed successfully |
181	| In-solution node doesn't resolve | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file, or `uip solution projects add` was never run for the agent project | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (same value as `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`) |
182	| Agent execution failed | Underlying agent errored | Check `$vars.{nodeId}.error` for details. For coded agents, test locally first with `uip codedagent run` |
183	| Empty `output.content` | Agent returned no response | Verify the agent is configured correctly (published: in Orchestrator; in-solution: in Studio Web) |
184	| `inputDefinition` is empty | Expected — agents accept input via flow wiring, not typed fields | Wire upstream data to the agent via `$vars` expressions |
185

1	# Coded Agents in Flow Projects (Sibling Folder)
2	
3	A coded agent can live as a sibling folder to a flow project inside the same solution. The flow references it via `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` with `section: "In this solution"`. The flow's `uip maestro flow registry list --local` discovers the agent by reading `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json`, written by `uip solution project add`.
4	
5	For the published-agent path (deployed standalone via `uip codedagent deploy`), see [coded/flow-integration.md § Pattern 2](flow-integration.md#pattern-2-published-coded-agent).
6	
7	## Sibling Folder Structure
8	
9	The `<resourceKey>` is the local UUID minted by `uip solution project add` — stable the moment the agent joins the solution.
10	
11	```
12	<SolutionDir>/
13	├── <SolutionName>.uipx
14	├── resources/                      # created and maintained by `uip solution project add`
15	│   └── solution_folder/
16	│       ├── process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json   # holds the `resource.key` UUID
17	│       └── package/<CodedAgentProject>.json
18	├── <FlowProject>/
19	│   ├── <FlowName>.flow
20	│   └── project.uiproj
21	└── <CodedAgentProject>/
22	    ├── main.py                     # agent entrypoint
23	    ├── pyproject.toml              # Python project config
24	    ├── uipath.json                 # UiPath project config
25	    ├── entry-points.json           # generated by `uip codedagent init`
26	    ├── bindings.json               # runtime bindings
27	    ├── main.mermaid                # generated graph diagram
28	    ├── project.uiproj              # Studio Web project metadata
29	    ├── .env                        # environment variables
30	    ├── .uipath/
31	    │   └── telemetry.json          # telemetry config
32	    └── .venv/                      # local virtualenv (created by `uv sync`)
33	```
34	
35	### Key differences from a published coded agent
36	
37	- **`resource.key`** is minted locally at `uip solution project add` time, not by Orchestrator at `uip codedagent deploy` time
38	- **No `codedagent deploy`** — the agent ships inside the solution package
39	- **Registry discovery is `--local`** (reads `resources/solution_folder/process/` files); no login or `registry pull` required
40	- **`model.section`** is `"In this solution"`
41	
42	## Scaffolding the Sibling-Folder Coded Agent
43	
44	The full end-to-end workflow (solution init → flow scaffold → agent scaffold → register → wire → validate) is owned by [`quickstart.md` § Scenario 2](quickstart.md#quick-start-scenario-2--in-solution-coded-agent-in-a-flow). This file covers the agent-side detail of step 3 (scaffold) and step 5 (registration) in finer detail; the canonical sequence stays in the quickstart so it remains executable in one pass.
45	
46	If the solution and flow project don't yet exist, run `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` and then `uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>"` from inside the solution **before** the steps below — those calls are the start of Scenario 2.
47	
48	1. From the solution directory, create the agent folder and scaffold inside it:
49	
50	   ```bash
51	   mkdir <CodedAgentProject>
52	   cd <CodedAgentProject>
53	   uv venv --python 3.13
54	   source .venv/bin/activate       # .venv/Scripts/activate on Windows
55	   uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>   # e.g. uipath for Coded Function
56	   uip codedagent setup --force
57	   uip codedagent new <agent-name>
58	   uv sync
59	   ```
60	
61	   For a simple stub with no LLM call, use the Coded Function framework
62	   (`uipath` package). This avoids downloading the full LangGraph or
63	   LlamaIndex stack and keeps the setup fast.
64	
65	2. Implement `main.py`. Use lazy LLM initialization (create clients inside functions, never at module level).
66	
67	3. Generate entry points:
68	
69	   ```bash
70	   uip codedagent init
71	   ```
72	
73	4. Register the agent in the solution — **this is the step that mints the `resource.key`** the flow will reference:
74	
75	   ```bash
76	   cd <SolutionDir>
77	   uip solution project add <CodedAgentProject> <SolutionName>.uipx --output json
78	   ```
79	
80	   After this command, `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json` holds the `resource.key` UUID.
81	
82	
83	### Flow Discovery
84	
85	From inside the flow project directory, the agent is discoverable via the in-solution registry. The `--local` flag tells the registry commands to walk up from CWD to find a `.uipx`, read the `resources/solution_folder/process/` files written by step 4, and surface every sibling project as a discoverable node type — all offline, without a tenant registry round-trip:
86	
87	```bash
88	# list every in-solution node type (all sibling projects)
89	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
90	
91	# fetch the full manifest for the coded agent
92	uip maestro flow registry get "uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>" --local --output json
93	```
94	
95	The second command's `Data.Node` object is what the flow skill pastes into the flow's `definitions[]`. For the node instance shape and top-level `bindings[]` entries, see [agent/impl.md § In-solution variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--in-solution-variant).
96	
97	Without `--local`, `registry list`/`get` query the tenant registry (Orchestrator-published resources only) and will not surface the sibling project.
98	
99	## Wiring the Agent's Inputs
100	
101	For inputs that reference flow variables, use `{ "type": "literal", "expression": "{{ $vars.X }}", "fieldType": "string" }` — NOT `=js:...` expressions. `=js:` ships as a literal string to the agent activity and fails at runtime with `Cannot find name '<identifier>'`.
102	
103	Input-only rule. Mapping the agent's output back to a flow-level global on an End node DOES use `=js:` — see [variables-and-expressions.md § Variable Updates](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md#variable-updates-variableupdates).
104

1	# Coded Agents — Flow Integration
2	
3	Coded agents in flows use the `uipath.core.agent.{key}` node with `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. Three patterns exist, distinguished by where the agent lives.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pattern 1: In-Solution Coded Agent
8	
9	The coded agent lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution as the flow. The flow references it with `section: "In this solution"`; the runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API.
10	
11	- **Agent-side scaffolding:** [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md)
12	- **Wiring the agent's inputs:** [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs)
13	- **Flow node JSON shape + top-level `bindings[]` + `definitions[]` entry:** [agent/impl.md § In-solution variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--in-solution-variant)
14	
15	The node-type's `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution project add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) and surfaced by `uip maestro flow registry list --local`.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Pattern 2: Published Coded Agent
20	
21	The coded agent is deployed to Orchestrator as a standalone tenant resource. Any solution can reference it.
22	
23	**When to use:** reused across flows, independent versioning, already deployed.
24	
25	```bash
26	uip codedagent deploy --my-workspace
27	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
28	```
29	
30	**Capture the package key from the deploy command's own output** — `uip codedagent deploy` prints JSON containing the package `Key` (an Orchestrator-assigned GUID). That GUID is the `resourceKey` used in the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey`. Always run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` after deploy to refresh the local flow registry cache, but do NOT depend on `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` to return the deployed agent — that search only enumerates built-in node types (`uipath.agent.autonomous`, etc.); user-deployed coded agents do not appear there, so an empty result is the *expected* state and is NOT a sign the deploy failed.
31	
32	Fallback discovery paths if the deploy output is unavailable or unparseable, **tried in order** — stop at the first one that returns the package:
33	
34	1. `uip or packages list --search "<agent-name>" --output json` (tenant feed listing). Returns 404 on tenants where the caller lacks `Orchestrator.Packages.View` scope — if so, move to (2).
35	2. `uip or processes list --folder-path "<FolderName>" --output json` if the agent was deployed via `--folder` rather than `--my-workspace`.
36	
37	If all paths return empty / 404, the deploy command's stdout JSON is authoritative — re-run the deploy and capture its output rather than chasing post-hoc discovery endpoints.
38	
39	For the flow node JSON shape, see [agent/impl.md § Published variant](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/impl.md#node-instance-inside-nodes--published-variant). `model.section` is `"Published"`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Pattern 3: Tool Resource for Another Agent
44	
45	The coded agent is a tool that another agent (inline or published) can call. Requires deploying the coded agent to Orchestrator first.
46	
47	**Resource file** at `<AgentProject>/resources/<ResourceName>/resource.json`:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "$resourceType": "tool",
52	  "type": "agent",
53	  "name": "MyCodedAgent",
54	  "description": "What this agent does (shown to the parent LLM for tool selection)",
55	  "location": "external",
56	  "properties": {
57	    "processName": "<CODED_AGENT_PROCESS_NAME>",
58	    "folderPath": "<FOLDER_PATH>"
59	  },
60	  "inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": { "userInput": { "type": "string" } } },
61	  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content":   { "type": "string" } } },
62	  "id": "<UUID>",
63	  "referenceKey": ""
64	}
65	```
66	
67	Coded agents use `location: "external"`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Pattern Comparison
72	
73	| Aspect | In-Solution (1) | Published (2) | Tool (3) |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Node type | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (local, from `project add`) | `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` (Orchestrator-assigned) | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` |
76	| Lifecycle | `uip solution upload` (single pass) | `uip codedagent deploy` | `uip codedagent deploy` |
77	| Runtime lookup | Studio Web projects API | Orchestrator Releases API | Orchestrator (via parent agent) |
78	| `model.section` | `"In this solution"` | `"Published"` or absent | n/a |
79	| Cross-flow reuse | No | Yes | Yes |
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Debug
84	
85	| Error | Cause | Fix |
86	| --- | --- | --- |
87	| Node doesn't resolve in SW (Pattern 1) | `resourceKey` was hand-invented rather than read from the resource file | Run `uip maestro flow registry list --local` and use the returned `resourceKey` (it matches `resource.key` in `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) |
88	| Agent not found in registry (Pattern 2/3) | Not deployed or registry stale | `uip codedagent deploy`, then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
89	| Tool resource never called | Tool description too vague | Sharpen the `description` in `resource.json` |
90

1	# UiPath Coded Agents — Quickstart
2	
3	For initial project scaffolding, follow [lifecycle/setup.md](lifecycle/setup.md) — it covers preflight, framework selection, starting points, and the workflow.
4	
5	## Project State Detection (run once, before step 1)
6	
7	Inspect the working directory and its ancestors. Compute the variables below — every later step branches on them. Re-running the flow is safe: each step is gated on these signals and skips itself when its work is already done.
8	
9	| Variable | How to detect | Used by |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| `project_state` | `local-workspace` if any ancestor contains `.sw-path-marker` or `.local/folder.lock` (Studio Web–specific markers — `*.uipx` alone does NOT qualify). Else `existing-coded` if cwd has `pyproject.toml` with `uipath` dep + a `<framework>.json`. Else `greenfield`. | Steps 1, 2, 3, 8, 9 |
12	| `framework` | Read from existing `<framework>.json` (`langgraph.json` / `llama_index.json` / `openai_agents.json` / `uipath.json` with `functions`). `none` if absent. | Step 1 |
13	| `has_venv` | `.venv/` exists in cwd | Step 2 |
14	| `has_entry_points` | `entry-points.json` exists | Steps 2, 6 |
15	| `has_bindings` | `bindings.json` exists | Step 4 |
16	| `has_smoke_set` | `evaluations/eval-sets/smoke-test.json` exists | Step 7 |
17	| `has_evaluators` | any `evaluations/evaluators/*.json` exists | Step 7 |
18	| `has_project_id` | `.env` contains `UIPATH_PROJECT_ID=<guid>` | Step 8 |
19	
20	When `project_state == local-workspace`, also read [lifecycle/local-workspace.md](lifecycle/local-workspace.md) for files-owned-by-Studio-Web and anti-patterns. 24	## CLI Conventions
25	
26	| Command family | Accepts `--output json` |
27	|---|---|
28	| `uip login`, `uip login status`, `uip login tenant list`, `uip login tenant set`, `uip logout` | yes |
29	| `uip codedagent setup` | yes |
30	| `uip codedagent new`, `init`, `run`, `dev`, `eval`, `deploy`, `push`, `pull`, `invoke` | no (forwarded to the Python CLI) |
31	
32	Use `uip codedagent <cmd>`, not `uv run uipath <cmd>`. The wrapper injects session credentials (`UIPATH_URL`, `UIPATH_ACCESS_TOKEN`, org/tenant identifiers) from your `uip login` session into the Python subprocess; `uv run uipath` skips that injection.

34	## Critical Rules
35	
36	- **NEVER add a `[build-system]` section to `pyproject.toml`**. No `hatchling`, no `setuptools`, no build backend. UiPath agents do not use a build system. Only include `[project]`, `[dependency-groups]`, and `[tool.*]` sections.
37	- **Always create a smoke evaluation set.** Every agent must include `evaluations/eval-sets/smoke-test.json` with 2-3 test cases covering the primary happy path (not exhaustive error-case coverage — the smoke set exists to catch regressions, not to fully validate behavior). Create it in the Evaluate step, not during Build.
38	- **Select a framework before writing any code.** If the prompt clearly implies a framework (e.g., mentions tools, RAG, multi-step orchestration, or a specific SDK), pick the best match. If the prompt is ambiguous, ask the user to choose from: Coded Function, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or OpenAI Agents.
39	- **Correct SDK import: `from uipath.platform import UiPath`** — not `from uipath import UiPath` (that path does not exist and will cause `ImportError`). Always instantiate `UiPath()` inside functions/nodes, never at module level.
40	- **Refresh the CLI's Python executable path after venv changes.** If `uip codedagent` reports that the UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or any error indicates a stale `uipathExePath`, activate the project venv and run `uip codedagent setup --force`. This rewrites the CLI configuration to point at the current `.venv` executable.
41	- **Auth check is one-shot.** Run `uip login status --output json` once, at step 5. If the user supplied environment + organization + tenant or explicitly asked to connect to a specific tenant, run the matching one-shot `uip login --organization "<ORG>" --tenant "<TENANT>" --output json` after the status check, even if another session is already logged in. Otherwise, the wrapper auto-refreshes tokens on subsequent cloud calls (no `uip login refresh` exists); re-auth only on a real `401`.
42	- **Use `uip codedagent run` from non-interactive shells.** `uip codedagent dev` auto-appends `--interactive`.
43	- **Runtime captures only the last node's delta as output.** `Annotated[list, operator.add]` reducers accumulate inside the graph but vanish from `--output-file` JSON and eval trajectories. Carry aggregate fields forward in each node's return (`{"items": [*state.get("items", []), x]}`) — see [frameworks/langgraph-integration.md](frameworks/langgraph-integration.md) § Runtime Output Quirk.
44	- **Verify the JSON, not the streamed display.** After `uip codedagent run --output-file out.json`, inspect `out.json` — the streamed view shows per-node deltas; the JSON is the runtime's actual final result. Mismatches expose the runtime quirk above.
45	- **Use `uip codedagent deploy` for packaging/publishing.** `uip codedagent pack` and `uip codedagent publish` are filtered by the wrapper.
46	- **NEVER run `uip login` without `--tenant`.** The interactive tenant picker does not work from Claude's Bash tool. Use the one-shot form `uip login --organization "<ORG>" --tenant "<TENANT>"`, mapping staging/alpha to `--authority` (see [../authentication.md](../authentication.md)).
47	- **Auth MUST be an interactive question only when needed and values are missing.** If the session check fails and the user did not provide all of environment / organization / tenant, your ENTIRE response must be a single direct question. Do NOT wrap it in bullet points, "Next Steps" headers, or status summaries. Just ask and stop:
48	
49	  > What is your UiPath **environment** (cloud/staging/alpha), **organization name**, and **tenant name**?
50	- **In a flow, coded agents are referenced via the [`agent`](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/plugins/agent/) plugin** — node type `uipath.core.agent.{key}`, `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. See [flow-integration.md](flow-integration.md) for the three patterns: in-solution sibling folder, Orchestrator-published, tool resource.

69	
70	Two top-level build paths. Pick one before starting — the lifecycle and publish mechanism differ.
71	
72	- **Scenario 1 — Standalone Coded Agent** — the agent is its own tenant resource, published via `uip codedagent deploy`. Use when the agent runs on its own, is called from multiple flows, or needs independent versioning.

Use when the agent is tightly coupled to one flow.

230	## Quick Start: Scenario 2 — In-Solution Coded Agent in a Flow
231	
232	Use when the coded agent is tightly coupled to one flow and lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution. The agent is wired to the flow via `--local` registry discovery — no separate Orchestrator deployment for the agent, no separate skill hand-off. **`uipath-agents` owns this scenario end-to-end** — solution scaffolding, flow scaffolding, agent build, registration, and flow wiring all happen here. Do not invoke `uipath-maestro-flow` as a separate skill; run the maestro-flow CLI commands directly from this workflow.
233	
234	Execute the following in order, end-to-end, in one pass — do not pause for confirmation between steps.
235	
236	1. **Scaffold the solution.** From the working directory:

238	   ```bash

240	   ```

242	   Creates `<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. All subsequent project paths are relative to the solution root.

244	2. **Scaffold the flow project inside the solution** (the layout is always double-nested `<Solution>/<Flow>/<Flow>.flow`):

248	   uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>" --output json
249	   ```
250	
251	   This auto-registers the flow as a project in the solution.

255	   ```bash

258	   uv add <framework-package>       # e.g. uipath-langchain for LangGraph
259	   uv add uipath-dev --dev

271	   uip codedagent init
272	   ```

296	   - Add a `uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>` node to `nodes[]` with one `inputs.<field>` entry per property in the agent's input schema (see step 6's `Data.Node.inputDefinition`) and `model.section: "In this solution"`.
297	   - For input field values, see [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs).
298	   - Add the definition from step 6 to `definitions[]`.
299	   - Add a top-level `bindings[]` entry for the agent (no duplicates per `(resourceKey, propertyAttribute)`).
300	   - Add edges from upstream nodes to the agent's input port and from its output port downstream.
301	   - To surface the agent's output as a flow-level result, declare an `out` global and map it on the End node with `"source": "=js:$vars.<agentNodeId>.output.<field>"` (outputs DO use `=js:`; only inputs do not).
302	
303	   See [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md) for the directory layout and [flow-integration.md § Pattern 1](flow-integration.md#pattern-1-in-solution-coded-agent) for the JSON shape.
304	
305	8. **Validate and format:**
306	
307	   ```bash
308	   uip maestro flow validate "<FlowName>.flow" --output json
309	   uip maestro flow format "<FlowName>.flow" --output json
310	   ```
311	
312	   Resolve any validation errors before declaring the scenario complete. Done when both commands return success and the flow file contains the wired agent node.

314	## Framework Selection
315	
316	> **First — is this an agent at all?** If the task is deterministic logic with no LLM reasoning (validate data, call an API with custom auth, transform records, upload/download files), it's a **Python Coded Function** — not an agent. Use the [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions) skill instead of this one. Coded Functions use typed I/O (`@dataclass`, Pydantic `BaseModel`, or a thin Python class with typed annotations) and a `functions` map in `uipath.json`; what distinguishes an agent is LLM reasoning and a framework graph.
317	
318	If the task needs LLM reasoning, infer the framework from the user's prompt when possible. If ambiguous, ask them to choose:
319	
320	1. **LangGraph** (recommended — best integrated with the UiPath ecosystem) — StateGraph with conditional routing, tool use, interrupts. Best for complex LLM agents.
321	2. **LlamaIndex** — Workflow with events and RAG support. Most complete LangGraph alternative.
322	3. **OpenAI Agents** — Lightweight agent with tools and handoffs. Best for simple LLM agents; lacks HITL, process invocation, and state persistence.
323	
324	**Inference hints:** mentions of tools/tool calling, multi-step, or orchestration → LangGraph. Simple handoffs or lightweight LLM → OpenAI Agents. No LLM needed → not an agent — use [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions). Summarize / research / synthesize over PDF or TXT (incl. bucket files, attachments) → not a framework choice — see [capabilities/deeprag/planning.md](capabilities/deeprag/planning.md). Per-row CSV extraction → see [capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md](capabilities/batch-transform/planning.md). When in doubt, ask.
325	
326	**Always tell the user which framework you selected and why** before proceeding to build. Example: "I'll use **LangGraph** for this agent since it involves tool calling and multi-step orchestration."

22	## Starting Points
23	
24	| Starting from | Use |
25	|---|---|
26	| Empty directory | The Workflow below |
27	| Existing UiPath agent (has `main.py` + `<framework>.json` + UiPath deps) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` only |
28	| Existing Python agent (has `main.py`, missing UiPath deps / framework config) | `source .venv/bin/activate`, `uv add <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>`, adapt `main.py` per the framework guide, then `uip codedagent setup --force && uip codedagent init` |
29	| Studio Web Local Workspace solution (ancestor contains `.sw-path-marker` or `.local/folder.lock`) | Already scaffolded by Studio Web. One-time local-run prep: `uv venv --python 3.13`, activate, `uv sync`, `uip codedagent setup --force`. Do **not** run `uip codedagent new`. Re-run `init` after every edit that adds/removes/renames/retypes a field on `Input`/`Output`/`State` or changes the entry-function signature — see [local-workspace.md](local-workspace.md) § Schema Sync After Edits for the full rule and anti-patterns. |

31	## Workflow
32	
33	```bash
34	mkdir <PROJECT_NAME> && cd <PROJECT_NAME>
35	uv venv --python 3.13                        # uv defaults to the latest Python; pin to a UiPath-supported version
36	source .venv/bin/activate                    # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
37	uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>
38	uip codedagent setup --force
39	uip codedagent new <PROJECT_NAME>
40	uv add uipath-dev --dev                      # required by `uip codedagent dev` (local dev web server)
41	uv sync
42	uip codedagent init
43	```
44	
45	`uipath-dev` is added to the dev dependency group during scaffold so `uip codedagent dev` works later without a second install pass. Skipping it causes `uip codedagent dev` to fail with *"The 'uipath-dev' package is required to use the dev command"*.
46	
47	**What `uip codedagent setup` does:** locates a Python that has `uipath` installed and caches its path, so later commands (`init`/`run`/`eval`/`pack`) can invoke the Python SDK. It searches PATH (`python3.x`, `python3`, `python`) and uses your `.venv` only when activated. So when using uv, always `uv sync` then activate the venv before the `setup` command.

49	## Coded Function Agents
50	
51	`uipath.json` carries the entrypoint mapping:
52	
53	```json
54	{
55	  "functions": {
56	    "main": "main.py:main"
57	  }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	Edit the scaffolded `main.py`'s `Input` / `Output` models and `async def main` to fit the real agent.
62	
63	## Generated Files
64	
65	| File | Purpose |
66	|---|---|
67	| `pyproject.toml` | Project metadata and dependencies |
68	| `main.py` | Agent entrypoint |
69	| `<framework>.json` | Framework config (LangGraph / LlamaIndex / OpenAI Agents) |
70	| `uipath.json` | Runtime options, pack options, `functions` map |
71	| `entry-points.json` | Input / output schemas from Pydantic models |
72	| `bindings.json` | Runtime bindings |
73	| `uv.lock` | Dependency lockfile |
74	| `.uipath/telemetry.json` | Telemetry configuration |
75	| `AGENTS.md`, `.agent/` | Documentation |
76	
77	## `uipath.json`
78	
79	```json
80	{
81	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
82	  "runtimeOptions": {
83	    "isConversational": false
84	  },
85	  "packOptions": {
86	    "fileExtensionsIncluded": [],
87	    "filesIncluded": [],
88	    "filesExcluded": [],
89	    "directoriesExcluded": [],
90	    "includeUvLock": true
91	  },
92	  "functions": {}
93	}
94	```
95	
96	**Key fields:**
97	- **`runtimeOptions.isConversational`** - scaffold defaults to `false` (single-shot). Building a chat/conversational agent? Flip to `true` BEFORE `uip codedagent init` so `entry-points.json` gets the chat shape. See [conversational-agents](../capabilities/conversational-agents.md).
98	- **`packOptions`** - Control which files are included when packaging for deployment
99	- **`functions`** - Entrypoint mappings (format: `"file_path:function_name"`)
100	
101	### `packOptions.directoriesExcluded` for solution context
102	
103	When the agent project is registered in a solution and uploaded via `uip solution upload`, the agent directory is bundled into the solution archive. Set `directoriesExcluded` to keep Python build artifacts out of the archive:
104	
105	```json
106	"packOptions": {
107	  "directoriesExcluded": [".venv", "__pycache__"],
108	  "includeUvLock": true
109	}
110	```
111	
112	`.venv/` is hundreds of MB of installed wheels and breaks uploads. `__pycache__/` is ephemeral bytecode. Both regenerate from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` on the target side. Without these exclusions, `uip solution upload` produces an oversized archive that can be rejected by Studio Web.
113	
114	- `isConversational: true` for chat-style agents.
115	- `packOptions` controls `.nupkg` contents at deploy time.
116	
117	## Troubleshooting
118	
119	| Error | Cause | Fix |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| `uipath executable not found` | `setup` not run, or run without venv activated | Activate `.venv` and re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
122	| UiPath CLI/Python executable is not recognized, or `uipathExePath` is stale | The CLI still points at an old or missing virtualenv executable | Run `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uip codedagent setup --force` to refresh `uipathExePath` |
123	| `Found .venv in current directory but no virtual environment is activated` | `.venv` exists but `VIRTUAL_ENV` is unset | Activate `.venv` first, then re-run `uip codedagent setup --force` |
124	| `No compatible Python installation found` | Python outside 3.11 – 3.13 | Install 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13 (or set `PYTHON_TOOL_PYTHON_VERSIONS`) |
125	| `Project authors cannot be empty` | Missing `authors` in `pyproject.toml` | Add `authors = [{ name = "Your Name" }]` to `[project]` |
126	| `NameError` during `init` | Framework not installed when `init` imports `main.py` | Run `uv sync` before `uip codedagent init` |
127	| `No entrypoints found in uipath.json` | Framework config or package missing | Verify `uv pip install` succeeded, then re-run `uip codedagent init` |
128	| `ModuleNotFoundError` for a package you just installed, even after activating `.venv` | A shell `python` alias points at a different interpreter (uv-managed, system, etc.) | Use `.venv/bin/python` directly for sanity checks, or `unalias python` for the session |

46	## Additional Instructions
47	
48	- **File/document input → `Attachment`, never a filesystem path string.** If the prompt says the agent "takes a CSV/PDF/file as input" (or similar), read `../capabilities/file-attachments.md` before defining the `Input` model. A `str` path field runs locally with `uip codedagent run` but breaks on Studio Web/Orchestrator, where no such path exists in the container.
49	- **Select a framework before writing any code.** Infer from the prompt if possible (tools/orchestration → LangGraph, RAG → LlamaIndex, simple LLM → OpenAI Agents, no LLM → Coded Function). If ambiguous, ask the user to choose.
50	- **Structured input contract → not OpenAI Agents.** OpenAI Agents always require a `messages` input field and cannot express an input contract without it (see `../frameworks/openai-agents-integration.md` § Input). When the user needs a strict typed/structured input (e.g. a single named field, no `messages`), choose LangGraph (custom `StateGraph` with arbitrary input state) instead. Do NOT silently fall back to a Coded Function to satisfy the input shape — a Coded Function produces `ProjectType: Function`, not a coded agent, so it does not fulfill a request for an agent.
51	- **Read ONLY the single framework reference** for the selected framework before writing code. Do NOT read other framework references or capability references unless the task explicitly requires that capability.
52	- **Clean generated scaffold code before schema init.** After `uip codedagent new` and before running `uip codedagent init`, inspect `main.py` and remove scaffold hazards: no module-level `UiPathChat`, `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI`, `UiPath`, or other auth-dependent clients; instantiate LLM/SDK clients inside graph nodes/functions only; ensure importing `main.py` works without UiPath auth.
53	- **NEVER instantiate LLM clients or SDK clients at module level.** `uip codedagent init` imports your Python file to introspect schemas — module-level `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()`, `UiPathChat()`, `UiPathChatOpenAI()`, or `UiPath()` will fail because auth may not have happened yet. Always create these instances inside functions or graph nodes, never at the top level of the module.
54	- **Correct SDK import: `from uipath.platform import UiPath`** — not `from uipath import UiPath` (that does not exist). Instantiate inside functions only: `sdk = UiPath()`.
55	- LangGraph agents get tracing automatically — no `@traced()` needed on graph nodes.
56	- Simple function agents require `@traced()` on the `main` function.

2	
3	Common implementation patterns for building UiPath coded agents, from coded functions to multi-agent orchestrations.
4	
5	> **Note:** These patterns are general architectural concepts. The code examples use **LangGraph** and the **UiPath Python SDK**. The same patterns apply to LlamaIndex and OpenAI Agents — see their respective integration references.
6	
7	## ⚠️ Before You Start: Setup Required
8	
9	**IMPORTANT:** Before implementing any agent pattern, you must first set up your project directory and install dependencies. This is a prerequisite for all agent types.
10	
11	See the **[Project Setup Guide](../lifecycle/setup.md)** for:
12	- Creating a new project directory
13	- Scaffolding with `uip codedagent new`
14	- Installing dependencies with `uv sync`
15	- Defining Input/Output Pydantic models
16	- Configuring your agent with `uip codedagent init`
17	- Testing your agent with `uip codedagent run`
18	
19	## Pattern Overview
20	
21	| Pattern | When to Use | Key Components |
22	|---------|-------------|----------------|
23	| [Simple Direct](#simple-direct-agent) | Deterministic logic, no external calls | `@traced()`, Pydantic models |
24	| [SDK Integration](#sdk-integration-agent) | Platform service calls (assets, queues, jobs) | `UiPath()` client, service methods |
25	| [LangGraph Workflow](#langgraph-workflow-agent) | Multi-step LLM reasoning with routing | `StateGraph`, conditional edges, LLM chains |
26	| [Human-in-the-Loop](#human-in-the-loop-agent) | Requires human approval or review | `interrupt()`, `CreateTask`, Action Center |
27	| [RAG](#rag-agent) | Knowledge retrieval and Q&A | `ContextGroundingVectorStore`, retrieval chains |
28	| [Chat](#chat-agent) | Conversational agents with tools | `create_react_agent()`, tool bindings |
29	| [Multi-Agent Supervisor](#multi-agent-supervisor) | Complex tasks needing specialized sub-agents | Supervisor node, worker agents, routing |

32	
33	## Simple Direct Agent
34	
35	Minimal agent with synchronous or async logic, no LLM calls or external services. Best for deterministic transformations, calculations, and data processing.
36	
37	**When to use:** Pure computation, data validation, format conversion, rule-based decisions.
38	
39	```python
40	from pydantic import BaseModel
41	from uipath.tracing import traced
42	
43	class Input(BaseModel):
44	    a: float
45	    b: float
46	    operator: str
47	
48	class Output(BaseModel):
49	    result: float
50	
51	@traced(name="calculate", span_type="tool")
52	def calculate(operator: str, a: float, b: float) -> float:
53	    match operator:
54	        case "+": return a + b
55	        case "-": return a - b
56	        case "*": return a * b
57	        case "/": return a / b if b != 0 else 0.0
58	        case _: raise ValueError(f"Unknown operator: {operator}")
59	
60	@traced()
61	async def main(input: Input) -> Output:
62	    result = calculate(input.operator, input.a, input.b)
63	    return Output(result=result)
64	```
65	
66	**Key points:**
67	- `@traced()` on `main` is required for Orchestrator visibility
68	- Use `@traced(name=..., span_type="tool")` on helper functions for granular traces
69	- Use `@mockable` from `uipath.eval.mocks` on functions calling external services so evaluations can substitute example calls
70	
71	---
72	
73	## SDK Integration Agent
74	
75	Uses the `UiPath()` client to interact with platform services like assets, queues, jobs, and buckets.
76	
77	**When to use:** Reading/writing Orchestrator assets, managing queues, triggering processes, uploading attachments.
78	
79	```python
80	import os
81	from pydantic import BaseModel
82	from uipath.platform import UiPath
83	from uipath.tracing import traced
84	
85	class Input(BaseModel):
86	    asset_name: str
87	    folder_path: str
88	
89	class Output(BaseModel):
90	    value: str
91	    status: str
92	
93	@traced()
94	async def main(input: Input) -> Output:
95	    client = UiPath()
96	
97	    asset = client.assets.retrieve(
98	        name=input.asset_name,
99	        folder_path=input.folder_path,
100	    )
101	
102	    return Output(
103	        value=str(asset.value),
104	        status="retrieved",
105	    )
106	```
107	
108	**Key points:**
109	- `UiPath()` reads credentials from environment variables by default
110	- All services support `folder_path` and `folder_key` for folder targeting
111	- Every service method has an async variant with `_async` suffix
112	- See [SDK Services](../capabilities/sdk-services.md) for the full API reference
113	
114	---
115	
116	## LangGraph Workflow Agent
117	
118	Multi-step agent using LangGraph's `StateGraph` with nodes, edges, and conditional routing. Supports LLM-powered decisions.
119	
120	> **Important:** LangGraph agents require `uipath-langchain` as a dependency and use a different project structure than coded function agents. See the LangGraph integration reference for project setup, `langgraph.json` configuration, and troubleshooting.
121	
122	**When to use:** Classification workflows, multi-step reasoning, conditional branching based on LLM output.
123	
124	```python
125	from pydantic import BaseModel
126	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph, MessagesState
127	from langgraph.types import Command
128	from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage
129	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
130	
131	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
132	    message: str
133	
134	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
135	    label: str
136	    confidence: float
137	
138	class GraphState(MessagesState):
139	    message: str
140	    label: str | None = None
141	    confidence: float | None = None
142	
143	async def classify(state: GraphState) -> Command:
144	    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(max_retries=3)
145	    result = await llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
146	    return Command(update={"label": "urgent", "confidence": 0.95})
147	
148	def route(state: GraphState) -> str:
149	    if (state.get("confidence") or 0) >= 0.8:
150	        return END
151	    return "review"
152	
153	builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
154	builder.add_node("classify", classify)
155	builder.add_edge(START, "classify")
156	builder.add_conditional_edges("classify", route)
157	graph = builder.compile()
158	```
159	
160	**Key points:**
161	- Use `MessagesState` for agents that need conversation history
162	- `Command(update={...})` to update state from nodes
163	- Conditional edges for routing based on state values
164	- LangGraph agents get tracing automatically — no `@traced()` needed on graph nodes
165	
166	---
167	
168	## Human-in-the-Loop Agent
169	
170	Extends a LangGraph workflow with `interrupt()` to pause execution and create an Action Center task for human review.
171	
172	**When to use:** Approval workflows, escalation paths, human review of LLM output, compliance checks.
173	
174	```python
175	from pydantic import BaseModel
176	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph, MessagesState
177	from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver
178	from langgraph.types import interrupt, Command
179	from uipath.platform.common import CreateTask
180	
181	class GraphState(MessagesState):
182	    label: str | None = None
183	    approved: bool = False
184	
185	async def wait_for_human(state: GraphState) -> Command:
186	    action_data = interrupt(
187	        CreateTask(
188	            app_name="review_app",
189	            app_folder_path="MyFolderPath",
190	            title="Review classification result",
191	            data={"label": state["label"]},
192	            assignee="reviewer@company.com",
193	        )
194	    )
195	    approved = isinstance(action_data.get("Answer"), bool) and action_data["Answer"]
196	    return Command(update={"approved": approved})
197	
198	def route_after_review(state: GraphState) -> str:
199	    return END if state["approved"] else "escalate"
200	
201	builder = StateGraph(GraphState)
202	builder.add_node("classify", classify_node)
203	builder.add_node("human_review", wait_for_human)
204	builder.add_node("escalate", escalate_node)
205	builder.add_edge(START, "classify")
206	builder.add_edge("classify", "human_review")
207	builder.add_conditional_edges("human_review", route_after_review)
208	graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())
209	```
210	
211	**Key points:**
212	- `interrupt()` pauses the graph and creates an Action Center task via `CreateTask`
213	- A `checkpointer` (e.g., `MemorySaver()`) is required for interrupt/resume to work
214	- `CreateTask` fields: `app_name`, `app_folder_path`, `title`, `data` (dict shown to reviewer), `assignee` (optional)
215	- Dynamic app folder paths require manual binding.
216	- The graph resumes when the human completes the action — return value comes from `interrupt()`
217
